reviews.text:
Makgeolli sold after its expiration date. I drank it all and figured it out. A senior I was eating with jokingly asked me to subtract the cost of makgeolli. What is this? Whether you're a part-time worker or something, isn't it absurd to say that it's okay to eat makgeolli past its expiration date?

Of course, it doesn't mean that you will get sick immediately just because the expiration date has passed, right? Usually, the expiration date is shorter than the period during which it deteriorates, so it is not a period for consumption, but the place where you work is clearly a registered business, and relevant laws stipulate that food beyond the expiration date cannot be sold.

Moreover, when I asked if the other makgeolli in the refrigerated showcase was okay, I was told that it would last until May 26th. (The day of visit was May 27th)

Sullae Gamjatang is a general restaurant, and as a business operator under the Food Sanitation Act, it must comply with its obligations.

Selling makgeolli that has passed its expiration date can be passed over as consideration for the self-employed, as the situation is difficult due to the coronavirus.

However, what was unforgivable was the employee's attitude. The owner will receive sales training every year, but I think you should also pay attention to training for your employees.

There is no need for an apology or compensation, and it is not being used for that purpose.

I just hope that failure to comply with the duties of a business owner will result in an administrative suspension of business (or alternatively a fine), and that the business will reflect on its actions and avoid such incidents in the future.

reviews.text:
The most important thing to consider when looking for a place to have a company dinner in Seongsu is the balance between atmosphere and food. If it's too loud, it's burdensome, and if the meat tastes average, there's no reason to gather. Marble Jeong, which has become known by word of mouth as a popular restaurant for company dinners in Seongsu, is a place that solves all these problems at once. The biggest strength is that you can enjoy high-quality Korean pork at a reasonable price in a sophisticated space like a wine bar.

When you enter Marble Jeong, you get a different impression from a typical meat restaurant. The lighting is soft and the table settings are neat, giving you the feeling of being in a restaurant or wine bar.

Even though it is a company dinner, it is not a noisy space, but rather a calm atmosphere where you can focus on conversation. This is an environment that will satisfy anyone looking for a restaurant with a good atmosphere in Seongsu.

The first assorted grilled Korean pork on the table gives off a sense of trust right from the looks of it. The pork belly and neck meat are properly composed, and the fat and texture of the meat are clearly visible.

You can check the freshness of Korean pork because of its unique bright red color and marbling. Even though it contains 600g, the price is not excessive, so it is easy to choose as a restaurant for company dinners in Seongsu. This place has a good balance between meat quality and price.

Another advantage of Marble Jeong is that the staff grills the meat themselves. The most cumbersome task at a company dinner is grilling meat, but here you can save yourself that effort.

First cook the thick meat on the outside over high heat, then adjust the temperature appropriately to retain the juices. Thanks to this, you can enjoy a properly cooked meal that is crispy on the outside and moist on the inside. It is impressive that consistent quality is maintained without any baking deviation.

What stands out as much as the meat is the side dishes. Fresh salads, vegetables, and pickled vegetables are neatly provided. It is a composition that brings out the natural taste of the ingredients rather than being spicy.

In particular, it can be eaten with a variety of vegetables to neutralize the fatty taste of meat. Even if you sit for a long time at a company dinner, you will feel less burdened.

A memorable element of Marble Jeong is the perilla leaf sauce. It has a different flavor from regular ssamjang.

The subtle herbal scent and savory flavor combine to take the taste of meat to the next level. If you put it on top of pork belly, it reduces the greasiness and goes well with pork belly. It is not just a side dish, but a point that shows the personality of this house.

If you have thoroughly enjoyed the meat, it is definitely worth ordering the soybean paste rice. The deep flavor of soybean paste is added to the spicy soup base, making it a perfect ending to a meal.

The combination of tofu, vegetables, and meat pieces makes it filling in just one bowl. The spicy taste eliminates greasiness and improves the completeness of the meal. One of the reasons why I recommend this restaurant for company dinners in Seongsu is this soybean paste rice.

A surprisingly important factor when choosing a venue for a company dinner is the bathroom. Marble Jeong has separate restrooms for men and women, and the interior is kept very clean.

Cleanliness of not only the tables and kitchen, but also the entire space is maintained, so you can rest assured even when visiting in groups. You can feel the operation paying attention to even the smallest details.

Marble Jeong is a place with a good overall balance, from atmosphere, meat quality, service, and side menus. Being able to enjoy high-quality Korean pork at a reasonable price in a wine bar-like space is a clear advantage.

Thanks to the staff-cooking system, you can focus on conversation even at company dinners, and the meal flows naturally with fresh side dishes, perilla leaf sauce, and soybean paste rice.

If you are looking for a restaurant in Seongsu for a company dinner, Marblejeong is an option worth considering. It is more suitable for places where you want to enjoy both atmosphere and taste.

The staff cooks it for you so you can taste it just right, and the fresh side dishes and perilla leaf sauce are impressive. Adding spicy soybean paste rice makes the meal more complete. Equipped with separate restrooms for men and women and a clean environment, it is recommended as a place for company dinners.

I ordered 2 servings of Eohwadungdung Sundaeguk.  The small old lady owner serves a pot full of sundae soup. I brought it home and put it on the gas stove and boiled it. The sundae was not the meat sundae I expected, but a vermicelli sundae. (In the photo, it looked like my father's meat sundae.) The sundae soup, which is full of head meat rather than sundae, is so savory and cozy that it brings back memories. You can add beef jerky and it tastes even better if you eat it with salted shrimp. I later found out that this place was considered a sanctuary in the surrounding area.  Not only do elderly guests come from far and wide, but believers from nearby churches also make it a rule to have lunch here on the weekends. As expected, there was a reason why I felt an unusual energy as I came and went. If you happen to be passing by nearby, it might be a good idea to visit. What was surprising was that there were more young customers. As expected, there seems to be no generational difference in taste. I wholeheartedly recommend Choyang Raw Meat Sundae Soup. ^^

Approaching its 1st anniversary, Hana Miyeokguk in Seongdong-gu delivers soul-warming, home-style miyeokguk that transformed my idea of the dish—sincere, healthy perfection. Since opening ~March 2025, I've made it my go-to for remote work lunches, pre-travel cleanses, or lonely evenings, where the rich broth, fresh vibes, rotating art (love that Monet-inspired seascape!), books, and soothing tunes heal everything.
Shy yet passionate owner infuses culture and creativity into every detail—ideal solo dining spot. Can't wait for year 2!

Note: Not suitable for vegetarians due to the beef broth.
Hanamiyeok Soup is already approaching its first anniversary.
As a local resident, I am truly grateful to be able to eat healthy, hearty meals.

I remember it opened around March 2025, and I think I always went there once or twice a month.
It was my first time eating seaweed soup here and I was impressed by the taste of the same sincerity I had at home.

I go there when I'm working from home and having trouble preparing dinner after work, before a long-term business trip or trip, or when I want to eat clean food after returning from a trip. And when I feel lonely, a bowl of warm seaweed soup and good music comfort me.

There are always new pictures and books. There is good music coming out. The owner always looks behind me. I tried talking to him a few times when there were few customers. Although he seemed shy, he was a dreamy owner who was very interested in art, music, and culture, and actually did things himself.

It's a great place to eat alone and enjoy a healthy and warm seaweed soup. I would like to continue visiting this year.

reviews.text:
A regular meat restaurant that I used to go to often.
The staff even grilled the meat themselves.
Every time I went, I had a good meal.
I went there often because it was close to my house.

One day, I went there and there were no customers, so I thought it was slowly closing down for business, so I asked if it was closed, and he said no and was accepting customers.
I ordered and waited as usual, but the meat came out later than usual.
But just looking at the meat that came out, the ratio of fat to meat was completely different from usual.
It's pork belly, but in some places it's mostly just fat and in other places it's just meat... Is it okay to serve something like this? I thought so.
Still, I visited several times and had good food, and since the staff cooked it for me, I just trusted it and waited for it to be finished.
After everything was baked, the employee left. I started eating with my girlfriend, but what I had hoped for turned out to be true.
The meat tasted completely different from usual.
You shouldn't sell it to customers... You shouldn't serve it as pork belly or pork neck... My girlfriend and I both felt the same way about King Lee, who thought they were selling the bad parts left over from the business to us.
I was going to ask and argue right away, but my girlfriend suggested that we just eat a little and go out.
Even in the middle of summer, I remembered the staff who were sweating and baking at the grilling place, and I also had good memories of that time, so I didn't say anything and paid the full price and left.
I won't be going here again after that.

What happens if you eat it deliciously many times?
If you hit a customer in the back once, will they think about visiting again next time?
This has been several years already.
The meat that was served to us... 'Can I serve this to you?' If they say they were worried or say, ‘Why don’t you apologize and give us some service?’ then I think it’s a restaurant with a real problem.
If the employee didn't know and accidentally handed it over without checking the status, I think it would be a bit of a blessing in disguise.
For the first time while reviewing restaurants on Google, I am giving the food 1 star.
Whether it was because we were playing with the food or it was a mistake, we ate that kind of meat and it remains a very bad memory.

The photo was taken when I was eating normally.

reviews.text: Sponsored // While looking for a good raw fish restaurant near Ttukseom Station, I ended up visiting Daemulhoe Pocha. It wasn't hard to find as it was a 3-minute walk from Exit 8 of Ttukseom Station, and I could see the open kitchen as soon as I entered the store, so I felt reassured in terms of hygiene and freshness. I ordered a plate of daemul raw fish, and was surprised at the generous amount of 4 types of aged raw fish, grilled fish, seasoned flying fish roe with vegetables, salt rice, mini stew, and sauce. The raw fish was fresh and of just the right thickness, so it had a good chew. The salmon and tuna, in particular, were so soft that I was impressed. The grilled fish was crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, so it was perfect to eat with rice. The salt rice adds a subtle umami flavor, so eating it with raw fish goes really well together. The mini soup had a refreshing broth, so it was a good way to end the meal, and there were a variety of sauces, so it was fun to choose according to your taste. Overall, it is a place that I would like to visit again next time because it is well worth the price and the taste is good.

I got there around 1 o'clock and finally finished eating (I was so annoyed that I wanted to go somewhere else, but my friends were coming from far away and there wasn't enough parking) so I ate meat. It says on the internet that break time is 3 o'clock. At 2 o'clock, I kept asking if I was going and they closed the door... I was disappointed. At the first store, they grilled meat and it was so delicious that I invited friends from far away to go there... If that's the case, just write that you don't sell meat for lunch and change the break time to 2 o'clock. They say banquet noodles are only for dinner... I used to sell food to office workers during lunch, but things have changed a lot. I'm not going anymore. I'm disappointed
